_comment: Randomized question pool. Prevention, not detection: if the agent asks the
same eight questions every interview, they end up on a forum within weeks
and we would be building a detector against a leak we created ourselves.
Selection is randomized per interview but the count per bucket is fixed, so
every candidate gets the same shape of interview.
'added' drives rotation age. Retire a question by setting 'retired' to a date;
retired questions stay here so old transcripts can still resolve their bucket.

questions.text: Which version of the main language or runtime were you on in that role?
How large was the dataset or request volume you were working with?
How many people were on the team you worked with most closely?
How long were you in that role?
What was your job title when you left?
Which cloud provider or hosting setup were you using?
Were you part of an on-call rotation, and how often?
What did you use for continuous integration?
How often did your team deploy to production?
What is the difference between optimistic and pessimistic locking?
In plain terms, what does an index do to a read and to a write?
What is the practical difference between a queue and a log?
Walk me through a project you owned end to end.
Tell me about a time you had to debug something in production under time pressure.
Describe a disagreement you had with a teammate about a technical decision.
Tell me about a mistake you made that had real consequences.
Describe a project where the requirements changed partway through.
Tell me about a time you had to explain something technical to a non-technical stakeholder.
Describe something you improved that nobody asked you to improve.
Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.
Describe how you divided up work on your last significant project.
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a deadline or a scope decision.
Describe a time you had to learn an unfamiliar system quickly.
Tell me about someone you worked with whose style differed from yours.
How do you think about the trade-off between shipping fast and building something maintainable?
How do you approach a codebase you have never seen before?
What makes a codebase hard to work in?
How do you decide what to work on when everything is urgent?
What does a good engineering culture look like to you?
How do you think about technical debt?
What do you look for when you review someone else's code?
What would make you leave a job?
What kind of problems do you want to be working on next?
How do you keep up with changes in the field?
What would you change about how your last team worked?
What questions do you have about how we work?
